The part's details from the parts table: Name="fwrd35-n2 RD Part B", Cost="$200.00", Markup="25%", Qty="1", Supplier="No supplier", Price="$250.00" ($200 cost × 1.25 markup = $250). The ticket's total row shows "Total (price × quantity) $375.00", which is the sum of Part A ($125.00) + Part B ($250.00).

Edited Part A on ticket RD-1015 successfully. The edit UI is triggered by clicking the "Edit" button on each part row, which opens an "Edit part" dialog pre-filled with the existing values (name, cost, markup, quantity, supplier). I changed Cost from 100 to 150, left Markup at 25% and Qty at 1, and clicked "Save part". The parts table now shows: **Part A** — Cost="$150.00", Markup="25%", Qty="1", Price="$187.50" ($150 × 1.25). **Part B** — Cost="$200.00", Markup="25%", Qty="1", Price="$250.00". The ticket's **total is $437.50** ($187.50 + $250.00).

Attempted to change ticket RD-1015 status to "Ready" by clicking the "Mark Ready" button. The app blocked it with a native alert dialog showing the EXACT error message: **"Ticket is not ready\nPart \"fwrd35-n1 RD Part A\" has no supplier\nPart \"fwrd35-n1 RD Part B\" has no supplier"**. The alert was titled "Ready?" on the button itself — clicking it triggers validation before committing. The ticket remains in **Draft** status. The page provides a hint: the Parts table has a "Supplier" column showing "No supplier" for both parts, and the "Mark Ready" button text suggests the app expects each part to have a supplier assigned before the ticket can proceed to "Ready" status.

Edited Part B ("fwrd35-n2 RD Part B") to assign supplier "Bench Supply Co" by clicking Edit, filling the supplier field, and saving. Both parts now show supplier "Bench Supply Co". Then clicked "Mark Ready" and accepted the confirmation dialog. The ticket status changed to "Ready". Part A: cost $150.00, markup 25%, qty 1, price $187.50, supplier "Bench Supply Co". Part B: cost $200.00, markup 25%, qty 1, price $250.00, supplier "Bench Supply Co". Ticket total: $437.50. Status: Ready.
